reviewed_lesson.reviewed_title: Telling time and arranging a meeting
reviewed_lesson.boundary_decision: Book pages 9-10 form one coherent sequence: page 9 establishes time expressions and page 10 applies them to schedules and arranging a meeting. Book page 11 changes the instructional focus to obligations/tasks (Things to do, including what someone has to do before playing football), so it begins the next curation boundary rather than remaining inside this time/meeting lesson.
boundary_evidence: book page 9 is titled What's the time? and its attached legacy question evidence concerns 12:15/quarter-past, minutes in an hour, and half-hour expressions
book page 10 is titled Arranging to meet someone and its attached legacy question evidence applies clock times to a schedule and a meeting time
the time expressions on page 9 are therefore prerequisite language directly applied by the meeting/schedule activity on page 10

book page 11 is titled Things to do and its attached legacy question evidence shifts to obligation/task language (for example, what Tom has to do before playing football), marking a distinct instructional focus

next_page_boundary_evidence.reason: instructional shift from telling time/arranging meetings to obligation and task language; treat as the next unresolved Lesson/Activity boundary
